reason: The fine blood vessels are shown delivering oxygen and nutrients to nerve cells, matching the remaining goal.
expectation: The vessels will supply the connected nerve cells with oxygen and nutrients.

effect: The blood vessels completed the nervous tissue and showed that nerve cells need a material supply as well as a way to communicate.
reaction: The distinction between signals in nerves and materials in blood was useful; the newly included supporting cells and fatty coverings were less explained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the prepared fibres to the receiving cells was most worthwhile: the picture traced a signal along a cell and a chemical message across the gap.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the blood vessels was straightforward but less engaging than assembling the signal path. The supporting cells and fatty coverings appeared without much explanation of their jobs.

surprise.text: I found it helpful that chemical messengers cross a small gap between cells, rather than the signal simply continuing through one unbroken cell.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt arbitrary; the pictures and goals pointed to the pairings. The supporting cells and fatty coverings did appear in the final tissue without being separately assembled.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see how these connected nerve cells help the body work, though this chapter's pairings were fairly predictable.
